title: So what versions of RPG Maker do you own and what versions do you still use?

posts.author: Garryg
posts.body:
What one do you primarily use and why?
I'd just be interested to see what most people here are developing for.
I've heard people say there is no reason to use anything except for the newest version and that they are all basically the same with the newest version just being 'better,' whatever that means to them!
I have to say that hadn't been my experience!
I may be weird but I have most (2000, 2003, XP, VX, VXAce, and MV) except for 'MZ' and the really early stuff  and I still like XP the best. Why?
Because it is very different from the rest for a variety of reasons, not the least of which is that it gives you direct access to the scripts, to do whatever you want with. I don't really like the direction the front-end editor has been going with most newer versions, I don't like the dumbing-down of what you can do with scripting. Plugins were a good idea and go a long way to stop people breaking the code. But the 'walled garden' approach is still restrictive compared to the 'anything goes' attitude of XP. Why diminish things like fogs and bitmaps, and multi level maps from the main editor for example?
Yes you can still do all this through writing a plugin, but what's the reasoning behind making you do that?
Should I bother getting MZ when it is on sale just to have a look? Is it significantly better/different from MV to use?
I haven't bothered looking at RPG MAKER UNITE. I have looked at UNITY itself but don't really have much interest.
Anyway I'd love to hear from anybody with an opposing view or from anyone who likes another older version best.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Garryg said:
I may be weird but I have most
Click to expand...
Probably more common than you'd think. RPG Maker goes on really big sales quite frequently, and since owning each version comes with the license to use the included assets anywhere, many people buy them just for that.
Personally I also own most of them.
I use MV to make my games and MZ to make the maps for my MV games due to the manual layer control. I own the rest just as a novelty and in the off chance someone commissions me for maps in an older engine.
Garryg said:
Should I bother getting MZ when it is on sale just to have a look?
Click to expand...
You should not. There's a perfectly usable demo on this site.
Personally I use MV because I prefer it over the MZ particle style animations. (I know you can do MV style ones now but the editor is buggy, and why bother when there's a perfectly usable MV already existing.)
I also prefer the way action sequencing works in MV compared to how they work with Visustella. I prefer the vast library of free plugins MV offers compared to MZ, although this is getting better over time as more people make MZ stuff.
Default asset wise, I really like XP, but I'm not about to mess around with an engine so outdated that I have to mess around with scripts just to get modern QoL. It's already bad enough with MV and RPG Maker in general, and I'm not going to bother upcaling them to 48x48.
Overall, the consensus seems to be if you're new, go with MZ, else just use whatever you like. At the end of the day, a great game can be made in any engine.

Javascript isn't an issue and once I got my head round what I was supposed to be doing (again very diferent from XP) I was fine. posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
I think I own all of them from 2k through MZ--but most of them are through Steam, and I haven't installed Steam on this computer because I was sick of the bloat XD Owning all of them means that you're clear to use resources edited from any of them, so--like Avery often says--it's the most economical DLC pack you could possibly buy.
I use and love XP. I love the default graphics style, I like the way tilesets are done, I like the way autotiles are done, I like that sprites have four columns instead of three because it lets me make smoother animations, etc. etc.. And, obviously, I have many years of experience with it that make it more comfortable for a casual hobby than having to learn another new thing. I also hit that "I could do this in a minute in XP, why can I not do this in a newer version?" stumbling block really quickly, get frustrated, and go back to old faithful XD
MZ is my second choice, because manual mapping layers make their triumphant return--I
hated
the auto-layer mapping. And since MZ lets you choose a tile size, I can keep using my 32px XP resources--but I've never done anything in MZ in any serious capacity, because I don't know what invisible hurdles I'm going to run into trying to use tall sprites when the engine was designed with chibi sprites in mind. Is there probably a simple solution out there? Yeah, probably. Have I had the brain bandwidth to seek it out? Nope. So I go back to old faithful again XD
At the end of the day, this is my hobby. I do it for fun, so I use the version that I like the best so that I can enjoy it the most.

posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
I have VX, VX Ace, MV and MZ. Currently I use MZ, and also MV to a lesser extent.
When I started with RPG Maker, there were two current options, XP and VX.  I downloaded the trials. XP looked better, but VX was much easier for a rank beginer. There were tutorials available, and there was the quick event creation feature that would do some basic events such as doors and transfers. At that time I didn't understand the concept of layers for maps.
A while later, VX Ace came out. It was quite a lot better, so I couldn't resist trying, then buying it.
When MV came out, I was a bit cautious at first. I tried it, and liked the bigger tile look. When I got used to it, I found that I prefered the plugin system to adding scripts in Ace.
Eventually I tried MZ. It does some things that MV would need a plugin for. (I do like my overworld sheet A forest autotiles to have '*' passability, for instance.) I like the feature that while you can just plonk tiles down in the same way as VX, Ace and MV, you can also look at and edit what is on each layer of the map. You don't always need to do that, but sometimes it is very useful. However, there are some things that I haven't found plugins for where the MV plugins don't work on MZ.

posts.author: Garryg
posts.body:
My buying was similar,  packs, sales and free. But I did look at each and they were not all just slight improvements on the last. Some took away things that were good as well as added!
Not to bang on but, XP was the big surprise for me, it looked and felt like it was made for a different audience with so much more directly exposed to the front-end!
MV is growing on me (a bit), but I've just been using it for a couple of weeks on and off and have already had to resort to making my own plugins to make (simple) stuff work.
So now I have a list of all the JS classes to see what they all do. It looks like most things you had before are still there but hidden from the user without programming, why?

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Here is what Zombie owns:
I have only used MZ because I game late to the game and didn't discover RPG Maker until about 3 years ago and I was already in my 50s.
So, learning one RM version and trying to learn Javascript is enough for one, poor, decrepit Zombie with limited time.
I own the other RMs for their assets.
I can't imagine trying to learn the other RMs when I can do everything I want in MZ and time I spent learning another RM could be invested in becoming more skills in Javascript, plugin making, or other game developing skills like trying to learn to make my own art assets.
I have to ask myself what interests me the most, what do I enjoy doing, what is the best return on my investment of time, etc.
I think it is completely different if you started with RPG Maker in the way back time and already have experience with multiple RMs.
Good luck on your projects and remember to enjoy what you do!
